payload.name: The Chaotic Caves
payload.description: "Fell monsters inhabit a network of caves on the borderland between savage wilderness and frontier civilization. Can the heroic adventurers root them out and save nearby towns and villages from attack?"
hooks: Treasure recovery and monster exterminators needed.
All goods recovered by lawful means from monsters become the property of the carrier.
Recently, monsters have become more numerous and sudden, savage attacks have occurred against locals.
Lizard men raid local shipping now and then, carrying off loot.
Most of the monsters being encountered are orcs, goblins, gnolls, and other lower-level creatures.
There is an old funeral crypt far off into the wilderness that the monsters are probably using as a base.
Human bandits are causing problems for outlying farms.
Some travelers have been attacked by Magic-User and Cleric spells.
People have been killed and eaten by ghouls near the crypt area.

town.name: Town
town.description: The town lies at the crossroads of a river and an old paved highway. It thrives on trade and commerce.
services: merchants offering food, clothing, and basic goods
docks with a narrow wooden pier
freight service with wagons and storage

areas.name: Front Door
areas.description: A large, round green front door to the halfling home.

areas.name: Living Room
areas.description: The main living room. It has a fireplace in the south wall and a round window about 4 feet in diameter in the north. There is no furniture. The room smells of death. A long-dead mauled body in rotten leather armor lies in the center; it carries a silver dagger in a belt sheath, 2 vials of holy water, 1 Potion of Healing, and a leather pouch with 3 cp. A tentacle worm lurks here and scuttles toward sounds in adjacent rooms, such as the front door being knocked in.

features.description: Small secret niche in the fireplace

areas.name: Dining Room
areas.description: A 15 by 17 foot dining room with two round windows in the north wall. Dust and floor discoloration show where tables and chairs once stood in the window light.

features.description: Two round windows in the north wall

areas.name: Kitchen
areas.description: A kitchen with a stone stove against the north wall and a chimney through the roof with a flue about 1 foot square. There are no other furnishings. A round window about 4 feet in diameter is in the northwest corner; its glass is broken out. A pool of slimy green water runs down the sill to the floor, looking exactly like a green slime monster but actually harmless.

features.description: Chimney with flue about 1 foot square
Round window in northwest corner with broken glass
Pool of harmless slimy green water on sill and floor

areas.name: Bedroom
areas.description: An empty bedroom with no furniture. It has a round window about 4 feet in diameter in the south wall.

areas.name: Bedroom
areas.description: An empty bedroom with no furniture. It has a round window about 4 feet in diameter in the south wall.

areas.name: Bedroom
areas.description: An empty bedroom with no furniture. It has a round window about 4 feet in diameter in the southwest corner.

areas.name: Back Door
areas.description: A simple round back door about 5 feet high with old, peeling red paint. It is barred from the inside and is old and easily knocked in.

areas.name: Tree House
areas.description: An old tree house, a simple square platform about 20 feet up from the ground and perhaps 6 feet from floor to ceiling. Fire beetles have taken up residence here and scuttle or jump down to attack.

features.description: Tree house about 20 feet above ground
Interior about 6 feet from floor to ceiling

areas.name: Stables and Storage
areas.description: A shed north of the house entered through double doors in another mound. The floor is dirt, the wall frames are heavy stone blocks, and the ceiling is made of heavy wooden timbers. The east, north, and west walls have round windows about 3 feet in diameter with shutters instead of glass; the north window is broken and smeared with splattered feces. Two empty pony stalls stand at the west end. The east end once held carts and stored goods. Several piles of once-sacked grain lie moldering under harmless yellow fungus. The floor is covered in stinking feces.

features.description: Round shuttered windows in east, north, and west walls
Broken north window smeared with feces
Moldering grain sacks covered in harmless yellow fungus

areas.name: Buried House
areas.description: A mound of earth overgrown with brush and weeds, unlike the other buildings. Square stones in loose earth near the main entrance suggest something buried here. Digging for an hour or two will reach the buried house. Searching on top reveals the small one-foot-square chimney to the fireplace in H12. All windows and doors are buried. The two main doors are boarded shut with a great deal of lumber, apparently out of fear.

features.description: Overgrown mound with brush and weeds
Square stones near main entrance hint at buried structure
Small one-foot-square chimney to the fireplace in H12 visible on top
All windows and doors are buried
Two main doors are heavily boarded shut

areas.name: Living Room
areas.description: An unfurnished living room with a brick fireplace in the northwest corner. Four humanoid shapes swaddled in cloth lie on the floor; they are zombies that rise and attack if anyone enters the home.

areas.name: Kitchen
areas.description: A kitchen crammed with two cozy chairs, a couch, a table, six wooden chairs, cupboards, a stove, and other furnishings.

areas.name: Master Bedroom
areas.description: The master bedroom contains a bed, dresser, and writing table. A zombie in tattered clothes sits behind the table; its exposed features are putrid and ragged from wounds and age. It attacks intruders with a flail used as a war hammer, growling in hatred of the living. The zombie has a massive hole in its back as if killed by a particularly brutal sword wound. Several sheets of old paper on the desk are covered with many different badly composed poems to "Kylenne My Lady Love" mixed with the name "Tyrok the Indefatigable." The writer was obviously disturbed and evil.

features.description: Old papers with poems to "Kylenne My Lady Love" and the name "Tyrok the Indefatigable"

areas.name: Guest Room
areas.description: A guest room containing a bed, table, small dresser, and a few other furnishings.

areas.name: Entranceway
areas.description: The cave entrance opens into crudely carved, cold, dark winding tunnels. Bones litter the grassy area outside, and large ogre-sized footprints can be found in muddy areas or soft soil. Deep enough inside the entryway to avoid sunlight are five thin cords strung across the width of the floor about 2' apart and an inch or two above the ground, covered by dust and hard to detect without close inspection. Some spikes on the released frame are covered in fresh blood and fur.

effect.manual: Five thin trip-cords release a broad frame pulled back against the east wall; it is 8' high and wide, lined with sharp wooden spikes, strikes as a 2 HD monster, and does 2d6 damage on a hit.

areas.name: Ogre's Lair
areas.description: An ogre is here, munching on the corpse of a bear. It might be bribed into helping the PCs if offered at least 200 gp, but it is incredibly dense and self-interested; it may attack intruders or lead a party in circles. It gets bored quickly and rarely stays with even an agreeable party for more than 1d6 days. The lair is furnished with hides, piles of leaves, and a few tree trunks used as benches. The ogre wields a large, knobby club.

features.description: Natural stone steps in the southwest hall descending 10'

areas.name: Gray Jelly's Pool
areas.description: Bones litter this wide, 3'-deep pool. The ogre occasionally takes body parts and throws them in to watch the gray jelly inside devour them. A plant-fiber cord is tied to a heavy rock on the edge of the pool; prickly spines along its length keep the ooze away from it. Tied to the other end is a heavy glass bottle that the ogre has thrown into the pool.

features.description: Plant-fiber cord with prickly spines tied to a heavy rock

areas.name: Steps
areas.description: Rough natural steps go down sharply some 20' in elevation to the north. They are coated in harmless slime.

features.description: Rough natural steps descending 20' to the north

areas.name: Steps
areas.description: Rough natural steps descend sharply some 20' in elevation to the north. Slime and pebbles coat them.

features.description: Rough natural steps descending 20' to the north
Slime and pebbles coating the steps

areas.name: Slope Down
areas.description: This slope goes down 30'.

areas.name: Stirge Rookery
areas.description: A long, narrow hole in the ceiling winds up some 30' to the forest floor above. Around noon light comes down in a dull glow through it. The ground is cluttered with feces and leaves, with worms wiggling in the leaves. Buried under the muck is a wooden chest holding the ogre's valuables from room C2.

features.description: Long narrow ceiling hole winding 30' up to the forest floor above
Ground cluttered with feces and leaves
Wooden chest buried under the muck

areas.name: Ornate Room
areas.description: A smashed-in door opens into a room carved out by human hands. It is furnished with a table, chairs, and a single skeletal figure sitting in a chair at the far end of the table. The ogre is deathly afraid of the room and will make an evil-eye sign if anyone gets near it.

features.description: Single skeletal figure seated in a chair at the far end of the table

areas.name: Cave-In Trap
areas.description: Noise and movement from the party will cause part of the fragile ceiling to collapse atop the first two or three party members. The collapse blocks the hallway and requires a half-hour's work to clear.

features.description: Collapsed rubble blocks the hallway until cleared with a half-hour's work

effect.manual: A cave-in triggered by party noise and movement collapses part of the fragile ceiling onto the first two or three party members; each is attacked as by a 2 HD monster for 1d6 damage on a hit, or as a 4 HD monster if not wearing a helmet.

areas.name: Cave Crickets
areas.description: Fungus and moss cover the floor and walls of this room. Cave locusts prowl here and will jump wildly if spooked.

features.description: Fungus covering the floor and walls
Moss covering the floor and walls

areas.name: Pool of Water
areas.description: A clear pool of water with a frog, a few small fish, and crayfish fills much of this chamber. Under the mud and muck at the bottom is a bone tube, and there is also a rotten pouch there. A rough iron ladder leads up into the ceiling through a tight hole 3' wide and exits in the woods 30' overhead.

features.description: Clear pool filling much of the chamber
A frog, small fish, and crayfish in the pool
Rough iron ladder leading up through a tight 3'-wide hole

areas.name: Crypt
areas.description: The entrance to an old tomb built of heavy stones buried under eons of dirt and brush. A rusted iron gate and door block the entranceway but can be pried open. Worn runes over the doorway bear Common slogans such as "EVIL WILL ALWAYS PREVAIL" and "DESTRUCTION TO ALL THAT IS GOOD." The tomb is a simple rectangle, 10' high, 20' wide, and 30' long from the door to the back wall. Inside are three stone coffins (sarcophagi). The main occupant lies in the middle sarcophagus and will avoid daylight, remaining inside until darkness falls.

features.description: rusted iron gate and door at the entrance

areas.name: Entrance
areas.description: Gaping cave entrance to Orc Lair A. Two orcs usually stand guard outside the entranceway, leaning on their spears. The first chamber inside serves as their usual bunk room.

features.description: First chamber used as a bunk room

areas.name: Empty Room
areas.description: A room whose walls and some of the ceiling collapsed some time ago; it is currently unfit to live in.

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: Quarters for a number of orcs, with their weapons and gear. Crude furniture stands in the center of the room, and wooden bunks line the walls. In the back are sacks of foodstuffs (potatoes, etc.) and hanging meat, with 12-72 pounds each of vegetables and meat.

areas.name: Wolf Pen
areas.description: Both ends of this area are blocked by a wooden fence spanning the complete width and height of the halls; in the center of each is a wooden gate about 3 feet wide and 6 feet high, lashed shut by rope. The wolves are usually alert and will raise a clamorous barking and howling if they hear or smell careless parties, which may attract wandering orcs and possibly the jailers in area 5. The soft earthen floor is littered with wooden bowls full of water, bones, and offal, but nothing else.

features.description: Wooden fence at both ends of the area
Two wooden gates, each about 3' wide and 6' high, lashed shut by rope
Bones and offal scattered on the floor

areas.name: Door to Jail
areas.description: Behind this door are the quarters for the big, sweaty orc who serves as warden of the jail and chief torturer, along with two assistants. Crude furniture and various simple wooden or stone interrogation devices fill the room. The key to the jail door is usually hung on a hide cord on the wall.

features.description: Simple wooden or stone interrogation devices
Jail key hanging on a hide cord on the wall

areas.name: Jail Area
areas.description: The locked door to the east opens into the jail, where anyone captured will be held. Currently there is a bedraggled merchant here, missing a finger that was sent off with a ransom note. If saved, he will give the party what he has at his home, though it is obvious the orcs think he is richer than he is.

areas.name: Chief's Room
areas.description: The strong, shrewd leader of the orcs resides here, sitting on a large, heavily-built throne when judging court. A sub-room to the south contains a bed and other personal furniture. His pets are also here: a mountain lion and two wolves. The tawny cat wears a collar with gems and is connected to a strong steel chain, usually attached to a steel hoop on the base of the throne; the chain can be released quickly. The wolves wear heavy leather collars and are usually chained to the wall beside the door. Usually there are four orcs here: two on permanent duty and two serving as messengers and go-fers. The chief has the key to the west temple door.

features.description: Large heavily-built throne used for judging court
Southern sub-room with bed and personal furniture
Steel hoop on the base of the throne for the mountain lion's chain
Wolves usually chained to the wall beside the door
Throne serves as a treasure chest with a flip-up seat

areas.name: Common Room/Guard Room
areas.description: Several orcs are housed here as a guard post against those in lair B. The room is cluttered with crude furniture and common foodstuffs, some in bags and some in the form of dried meats hanging on strings.

areas.name: Pools
areas.description: These pools of water are fed by underground springs. They provide a year-round source of fresh water. They are 6 feet deep and clean, but otherwise not unusual.

areas.name: Shared Hallway
areas.description: At each end of this hallway is a heavy, thick wooden door bound by strong steel bands, with crafty and heavy locks. Each of the orc chiefs in rooms 6 and 13 has the key to the opposite side, and they must cooperate to enter the temple. The orcs on either side had been fighting so savagely for the affections of the god in the temple that a high priest had the doors locked and gave the keys to the chiefs, warning them against any further misconduct.

features.description: Heavy thick wooden door at each end of the hallway
Strong steel bands on both doors

areas.name: Orc Temple
areas.description: This temple was carefully cut from the living stone and is well-maintained. Four pillars are fluted and ornate, and the floor is tiled with polished green and red marble. The ceiling rises some 20 feet high. On a dais about 6 feet above the floor stands a 12-foot-high statue of a vindictive, evil orc god, carved from a single shining piece of black basalt. No steps are provided for getting atop the dais; no one is supposed to stand on it.

features.description: Polished green and red marble floor
12' high black basalt statue of an evil orc god

areas.name: Entrance
areas.description: The first chamber of Orc Lair B has four orcs immediately inside along with a hobgoblin who joined the orcs after looking for greener pastures. These orcs share duty guarding the local orc temple and have a cruel sense of humor. Each inhabitant has 1d6 sp.

areas.name: Secret Safe Room
areas.description: Only the orc chief in room 13 knows of this secret room. The main chamber contains a cot, food, flint and steel, a skin of water, and a cloak.

effect.manual: Both secret doors into the room are very well hidden and each is trapped in two ways: opening one without disarming it releases gas causing anyone within 10 feet to save vs. Poison or fall asleep for 1d6 hours, and also sounds an alarm loudly for 1 minute in the chief's quarters.

areas.name: Guard Post
areas.description: Two orcs with spears and hand axes stand guard at this door. The short corridor between this room and the next room provides a buffer zone in case of attack. Each guard has 1d6 sp.

features.description: Short corridor serving as a buffer zone in case of attack.

areas.name: Chief's Quarters
areas.description: The wily orc chief resides here, usually with a war leader and two common orcs. The chief has a key to the eastern temple door at room 9 attached to a necklace of long pencil-thin gold bars worth 100 gp. The room contains stout wooden furniture. Under a heavy chair in the northeast corner is the alarm bell that rings if either trapped secret door in room 11 is opened without being disarmed first.

features.description: Alarm bell under a heavy chair in the northeast corner linked to the trapped secret doors of room 11.

effect.manual: A locked chest has a gas trap inside. When opened without inserting a long pencil-sized object into a hole in back, it releases gas in a 10-foot area; affected creatures save vs. Poison or die (or suffer a similarly nasty effect at the GM's option).

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: This trash-littered room houses nine orcs. They are currently throwing rocks at one who is standing against a wall while several others are bruised; the game is to see who can take the most beating before flinching. Each has 1d6 sp.

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: This room houses seven orcs. It is cluttered with miscellaneous debris they have torn up and discarded, as well as firewood and stone circles for cooking.

features.description: Hidden hole in the northeast corner concealed by fireplace rocks and a foot of earth.

areas.name: Entrance
areas.description: Twin entrances lead into the first chamber, where five hobgoblins are bunked on guard duty. At A is a wide underground stream used as a moat. Wooden planks about 15' long, used to cross it, are stored on the opposite side. A loud ox horn hangs on a peg and can be blown to attract someone to come put planks across; the hobgoblins in room 17 are tasked with this job. If intruders spend too long debating or making elaborate crossing plans, two hobgoblins from room 17 may appear. In the northwest corner at C is a crude hide painted to resemble stone, used for ambushes by hiding behind it and rushing out once intruders enter.

features.description: Wide underground stream used as a moat
Wooden planks about 15' long stored on the far side for crossing
Loud ox horn on a peg to summon hobgoblins from room 17 to lay the planks
Crude stone-painted hide in the northwest corner used for ambushes

areas.name: Trapped Hallway
areas.description: A 20' high hallway supported by three sets of pillars. The hobgoblins have rigged thin wires along the floor between the center two pillars.

features.description: Bell-covered net spanning the hall between the center pillars

effect.manual: Thin floor wires trigger a heavy stone-headed mallet swinging down from behind the pillars; it attacks as a 2 HD creature and deals 1d8 damage on a hit. A moment later a net covered in bells drops across the hall between the two pillars. Anyone caught is tangled for 1d6 rounds, and struggling causes the bells to ring loudly, likely alerting hobgoblins from room 17.

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: Six hobgoblins bunk here. They are not wearing armor but will don it if given time. The room has been fixed up, and what were once going to be platforms for caskets are now used as benches and tables. Three fancy elaborate red funeral shrouds with thin gold threading and black details are being used as hammocks.

features.description: Former casket platforms repurposed as benches and tables
Three elaborate red funeral-shroud hammocks with thin gold threading and black details

areas.name: Store Room
areas.description: Usually this room is locked, though not very well. A thief could pick either door with ease, and the doors can be knocked in easily. The chief in room 21 has the key. It is full of odds and ends and minor plunder: clothing, sacks of grains and potatoes, hanging dried meats, perhaps some hanging 'fresh meat' in the form of slain foes, and mining tools such as picks, chisels, and hammers.

features.description: Possibly hanging slain foes used as 'fresh meat'
Mining tools including picks, chisels, and hammers

areas.name: Sub-Leader
areas.description: This room has been taken over by a skilled and tough hobgoblin who lives in luxury. On the wall are a short bow and two quivers of arrows, along with other items. He carries the key to this room on a string made of hair on his belt.

features.description: Two quivers of arrows on the wall

areas.name: Guard Room
areas.description: The hobgoblins here have piled up rubble in the hallway and stockpiled holy water to fend off the ghouls to the west.

features.description: Rubble piled up in the hallway as a defensive barrier

areas.name: Chief's Room
areas.description: This chamber contains the hobgoblin chief and three bodyguards. The chief has the key to the store room at 18. There is a plain bed, chairs, tables, and other furnishings here.

areas.name: Ghouls
areas.description: Three ghouls lurk here trying to get through the rubble to the hobgoblins in #20. They are not interested in skeletons or zombies as a possible food source.

areas.name: Skeletons
areas.description: Six skeletons, three on the east and three on the west, stand like guards stiff at attention and attack intruders on sight.

areas.name: Zombies
areas.description: Zombies wait patiently here under orders to attack and destroy any intruders.

features.description: Splinters of what appears to have been an ornate cabinet

areas.name: Skeletons
areas.description: The skeletons posted here attack on sight. The outward-facing walls are lined by crypt spaces (3 high, 3 wide per 10' section); many are empty. Those with anything in them have the remains of poor people. Hanging out the gaping square of one crypt space in plain sight is a necklace with gems worth 750 gp; the original owners will be so glad to have it recovered as a sentimental heirloom that they will pay 1,000 gp for it, if they are tracked down.

features.description: Outward-facing walls lined by crypt spaces, 3 high and 3 wide per 10' section
Some crypt spaces contain the remains of poor people

areas.name: Guard Post
areas.description: A dark, dank goblin guard post in the crudely tunneled warren. Six goblins hunker here ready to fight intruders. Each carries 1d6 cp. They control a net trap at the lair entrance by jerking a rope; if intruders try to free trapped companions, the goblins pelt them with slings.

effect.manual: A net trap covers the marked entrance area. The goblins can drop it by pulling a rope. Entangled victims are easily subdued but can free themselves in 1d6 rounds if left alone; those walking directly under it are very likely to be caught.

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: A common room whose entrance is covered by crude curtains made from rawhide and cheap cloth. Inside, seven unarmored goblins rest on simple but well-made wooden furniture: stools, tables, cots, and bedding of common furs. Each carries 1d6 cp.

features.description: Crude rawhide and cheap-cloth curtains over the entrance.
Simple but well-made wooden stools, tables, cots, and bedding of common furs.

areas.name: Trap
areas.description: A cleverly concealed pit trap in the goblin lair.

effect.manual: A 10-foot-deep pit trap. Victims take 1d6 damage from falling. The covering is cleverly made; even tapping for a hollow floor only reveals a faint noise on a standard trap-finding check.

areas.name: Goblin Priest
areas.description: The room of an old goblin who serves as spiritual adviser to the chief and tribe. He is wise but petty and cruel, and misguides others for his own profit. He is not truly a cleric and cannot use the scroll found here. He does not have armor.

areas.name: Common Room/Store Room
areas.description: A combined common room and store room occupied by unarmored goblins. Large wicker baskets are stacked along the back wall, filled with wheat grain, flour, vegetables, dried meats, and other items. Each goblin carries 1d6 cp.

features.description: Large wicker baskets stacked along the back wall, filled with wheat grain, flour, vegetables, dried meats, and other items.
Six beautiful 1-foot-tall statues in niches in the southeast wall.

areas.name: Goblin Chief Room
areas.description: The goblin chief's room, inhabited by the chief and three other goblins. The chief wields a Shortsword +1. The north, south, and east walls are covered by curtains assembled from a hodgepodge of bed linens, tapestries, and hides. A concealed cache is buried in the southeast corner under a clever covering that requires a find secret door check or equivalent search to locate.

features.description: Curtains on the north, south, and east walls made from mixed bed linens, tapestries, and hides.
Overturned bucket in the northeast corner hiding a bag of coins.
A buried hidden cache in the southeast corner beneath a clever covering.

areas.name: East Entrance
areas.description: East entrance to the bandit lair, out of sight from the west entrance in the woods. Four humans and a dwarf stand guard here; on hot days they take cover just inside the cave entrance. Each guard has a crossbow and a case of bolts that are traded out as the guard changes. At night, a dozen torches are kept just inside the entrance along with a covered bowl of hot coals.

features.description: Dozen torches kept just inside the entrance at night

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: Common room where six human fighters are bunked. The furniture is light and easy to break down and move, but not very sturdy. The room is lit by two common oil lamps, and oil is brought in with a wooden cup when needed.

areas.name: Locked Store Room
areas.description: Locked store room containing provisions and loot from raids. The door is heavy and locked; knocking it in will take some time. The deputy to the leader in room 41 usually has the key. A well has been driven down for water.

features.description: Large clay jug holding eight gallons of lantern oil

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: Common room where six bandits reside. The room is lit by two common oil lamps, and oil is brought in with a wooden cup when needed.

areas.name: Leader's Room
areas.description: Leader's room. The bandit leader and two main cronies are here, seated at a table looking over a map of the general area with notes about the best prospects for ambushing traders. The room has a lantern on a swinging hook with a continual light spell cast inside it; it is kept fueled in case the spell is dispelled or countered by continual darkness. The captain has the key to the storage room at 40, the key to the locked strongbox, and a ring of keys for the dungeon doors at 38.

features.description: Table with a map of the general area and ambush notes
Wooden jar holding a gallon of lantern oil
Continual light spell cast inside the lantern
Leader carries ring of keys to the dungeon doors in room 38

areas.name: Stables
areas.description: Stables where the bandits keep their animals hidden, taking them out to browse during the day. The dotted lines on the map are wooden fences, with gates where needed. In one corner are a wagon, two saddles and bridles, and two sets of saddlebags; the wagon also holds several large bags of grain, buckets, and other items.

areas.name: Dungeon
areas.description: Dungeon used as a holding area for captives and anyone the captain wants to throw into irons. The captain currently has the keys in room 36. Cell a holds three merchants, all noncombatants; if rescued and returned to town, one offers a necklace with gems worth 100 gp and the other two offer 100 gp each. Cell b is empty. Cell c contains a recalcitrant bandit imprisoned for pilfering and bad-mouthing everyone; she will try to ingratiate herself by posing as a merchant's guard, then steal what she can and run off. She has no armor and no weapon. Cell d holds drink stores. Cell e is empty.

features.description: Captain in room 36 has the keys
Cell d: three jars of good wine, two jars of cheap wine, and a dozen bottles of ale in a box

areas.name: Guard Post
areas.description: Guard post where three men are always stationed to guard the main loot, with strict instructions about who to let in. A common oil lamp provides light.

areas.name: Treasure Room
areas.description: Treasure room where the best loot is stored behind a strong, locked door. The bandit captain in room 36 keeps the key.

areas.name: Bandit Lieutenant
areas.description: Quarters shared by the bandit leader's deputy and cronies, though the cronies are usually with the leader in room 36. The lieutenant is an elven thief wearing leather armor and carrying a dagger and shortsword; a shortbow and quiver of arrows hang on a peg by the door. The main room has tables, couches, and normal living furnishings. The three back rooms (41a, 41b, and 41c) contain beds and other personal items. All furniture is crude and handmade from local materials. Each room has a plain oil lamp, and the main room has a wooden jug with a quart of oil. The lieutenant usually has the key to room 34.

features.description: Shortbow and quiver of arrows on a peg by the door
Three back rooms (41a, 41b, 41c) with beds and personal items
Plain oil lamp in each room
Wooden jug with a quart of oil in the main room

areas.name: West Entrance
areas.description: West entrance to the bandit lair, out of sight from the east entrance in the woods. Four humans and a halfling stand guard here; on hot days they are usually inside the cave entrance. They have crossbows and a case of bolts which are traded out as the guard changes. A dozen torches are kept just inside the entrance along with a covered bowl of hot coals.

features.description: Dozen torches just inside the entrance

areas.name: Guard Post
areas.description: Nine kobolds hunker nervously here. South of them is a locked storeroom; the chief in room 48 has the key. The storeroom contains dried meat, pickled vegetables in clay jars, and other supplies.

features.description: Locked storeroom to the south containing dried meat, pickled vegetables in clay jars, and other supplies

areas.name: Guards
areas.description: Seven kobolds lounge on benches and chairs around tables. None have armor.

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: The doors to this room are made of flimsy wooden poles lashed together; they can be kicked in or heard through easily. A number of the kobolds inside keep normal rats as pets, though they eat their pets now and then. None of the kobolds have armor.

features.description: Flimsy pole-lashed doors that can be kicked in or heard through easily

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: The door to this room is rickety and easily kicked in or listened through. The kobolds inside do not have armor. Ordinary rats and mice scurry among the litter; some are being cooked on a fire.

features.description: Rickety door that is easily kicked in or listened through
Fire with some rats and mice being cooked

areas.name: Trophy Room
areas.description: This open chamber is decorated with old metal helmets, clothing hung on wooden frames like scarecrows, and other items. These are all mementos of opponents defeated in battle. Most are unimpressive, and some are kobold-sized. A well-hidden secret door in the center of the west wall opens by taking a careful grip on one side and pulling; only the chief knows it is there.

features.description: Clothing hung on wooden frames like scarecrows

areas.name: Chief's Room
areas.description: The kobold chief, two bodyguards, and four normal kobolds live here. The chief has the key to the storeroom at 43.

features.description: Large clay urn in back with a wooden lid tied on by rough fiber rope

areas.name: Escape Route
areas.description: As shown on the map, a pit trap with stakes lies about 10 or 20 feet from the entranceway, covered by a pretty good false floor, though a careful search should have a high chance of finding it. The outside exit is in the middle of the woods and has been covered by living brush and debris so that it is hard to find. Scuttling in the brush just outside the entrance are seven giant centipedes that attack anyone who comes near.

features.description: Concealed outside exit in the middle of the woods, hidden by living brush and debris

effect.manual: Pit trap with stakes about 10 or 20 feet from the entranceway, hidden by a false floor; falling in causes 2d6 damage.

areas.name: North Entrance
areas.description: North entrance to the lizard man lair. Two totem poles flank the rough entrance clawed into hard, rocky ground; each is capped with a bleached bear skull and feathers. The tunnel slopes down sharply from the opening to the first chamber, dropping about 30 feet in elevation. Several boulders here can be rolled into the hallway and packed with mud to prevent flooding.

features.description: Two totem poles capped with bear skulls and feathers
Several boulders that can be rolled into the hallway and packed with mud to prevent flooding

areas.name: Empty Chamber
areas.description: An empty chamber stacked with firewood, dry grass for tinder, and rocks.

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: Common room serving as the residence of three male lizard men; they are unarmored.

areas.name: Larder (Food Storage)
areas.description: These two chambers are separated from each other and the hallway by reed walls about 3 feet high. The western pool is 2 feet deep and contains fish, eels, crawdads, and similar creatures; the other chamber contains turtles, lizards, and rabbits.

features.description: Two chambers divided by 3-foot-high reed walls
Western pool 2 feet deep containing fish, eels, crawdads, and similar creatures
Other chamber containing turtles, lizards, and rabbits

areas.name: Main Harem
areas.description: Main harem of the lizard men. The leader resides here with two prime female mates, statistically indistinguishable from males, and six young. Other than the leader, all are unarmored. The leader wears armor of tough hide and bone and has a 100 gp gem on a thong around his neck marking him as dominant instead of the usual 25 gp gem. A leather sack with a drawstring is hidden in a hole in the center of the north wall, covered over by mud. Two hollow tree trunks about 1 foot in diameter rise through the roof and exit above, providing ventilation. If cornered here, the lizard men can dig out through the ceiling, taking perhaps an hour or less. A fire smolders in one corner with several large rats smoking over it. Smoked meats, vegetables, and other items are piled beside them. Several large, well-made hard-baked clay pots and jars are here, along with hides and furs stacked along one wall, plus firewood, grasses, and leaves for bedding and fires. Hanging on a peg on the wall is a reed whistle, a Whistle of Summoning Animals, which can be blown three times total; each use summons normal local animals for 2d6 turns.

features.description: Hidden hole in the center of the north wall covered with mud
Two hollow tree trunks through the roof providing ventilation
Ceiling can be dug through for escape
Smoldering fire with several large rats smoking over it
Piles of smoked meats and vegetables
Several large hard-baked clay pots and jars
Hides and furs stacked along one wall
Firewood, grasses, and leaves for bedding and fires
Peg on wall holding a reed whistle

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: Common room where three male lizard men are busy readying simple bamboo gigs for a fish-and-frog hunt.

features.description: Simple bamboo gigs for a fish-and-frog hunt

areas.name: Guard Post
areas.description: Guard post where three lizard men wearing tough hide and bone armor and a giant gecko lizard on a thick fiber rope lurk in the dark, keeping intruders, including animals, out. The tunnel slopes down sharply from the opening to here, dropping about 30 feet. Several boulders here can be rolled into the hallway and packed with mud to prevent flooding.

features.description: Several boulders that can be rolled into the hallway and packed with mud to prevent flooding
Thick fiber rope for the giant gecko lizard

areas.name: South Entrance
areas.description: South entrance opening into the bank of the stream, about 20 feet high here. It is flanked by two 9-foot totem poles featuring crude animals and lizards, capped by bear skulls and feathers.

features.description: Two 9-foot totem poles featuring crude animals and lizards, capped by bear skulls and feathers
Entrance opens into the stream bank 20 feet high

areas.name: Entrance
areas.description: Entrance to the bugbear lair. Two bugbears with pole arms stand outside the entranceway, one on each side, and another waits in the niche just inside. Heavy wooden beams support the lair ceilings; most ceilings in the lair are 15 feet high.

features.description: Ceilings generally 15 feet high in the lair

areas.name: Swinging Arm Trap
areas.description: A trapped hall with protection at both ends. A swinging frame set with sharp, hard wooden spikes slashes out when a pressure plate is stepped on, potentially hitting each person in front.

features.description: Swinging spiked wooden frames at both ends of the hall

effect.manual: Pressure plate triggers a swinging spiked wooden frame at either end of the hall; it attacks as a 2 HD monster and deals 2d6 damage to each person hit.

areas.name: Store Room
areas.description: Store room. The door is open. Just inside hangs a tarp meant to block light, but its west side has been carefully cultured with yellow mold so that anyone pushing brusquely through releases spores. The bugbears use a pole to lift the tarp aside from a distance. The room contains crates of food, bags of meat, three 50-foot sections of rope, a dozen iron spikes, and other items.

features.description: Hanging tarp just inside the room

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: Common room occupied by three bugbears. The east wall is decorated with three long strips of cheap paper covered in bugbear writing: prayer scrolls pleading for success in battle and many enemies to feast on.

features.description: Three prayer scrolls on the east wall written in bugbear script

areas.name: Empty Common Room
areas.description: An empty common room with benches and tables stacked on the north wall and bunks and boxes on the south wall.

features.description: Benches stacked on the north wall
Tables stacked on the north wall

areas.name: Secret Door
areas.description: A well-hidden secret door. It opens only when a block in the ceiling overhead is gripped and pulled down; the door swings up, and the latch is reset when it is swung down. This hidden access conceals the prison and main treasure room; captives are blindfolded before entering or exiting to preserve the secret.

features.description: Ceiling block trigger that opens the secret door
Door swings up and resets when swung down

areas.name: Treasure Room
areas.description: Treasure room. The door is extremely strong and secured with a high-quality lock; the chief in room 68 has the key. A small niche in one side of the door frame contains a latch. Unless someone inserts a blade or similar tool and presses the latch, a bladder over the door releases gas outside the door when it is opened. The room contains chests, boxes, and barrels.

features.description: Small niche in the door frame concealing a latch

effect.manual: Opening the door without pressing the hidden latch in the door-frame niche releases gas outside the door; if open flame is nearby it ignites and deals 1d6 damage to all within 10 feet (save vs. Dragon Breath for half). Without flame, the gas is harmless and dissipates in 1d6 turns.

areas.name: Prison
areas.description: Prison. The head jailer is usually in and around area "e" with an assistant. Heavy wooden doors to cells a through d are locked and have barred windows for inspection. Area e is a torture room with stools for guards, iron loops and chains on the walls for victims, and a hot brazier and fireplace poker kept ready at all times. Cells a and d are empty. Cell b holds a desperate merchant. Cell c contains two completely harmless human or elven skeletons.

features.description: Locked heavy wooden cell doors for cells a-d
Barred windows in the cell doors
Iron loops and chains on the walls
Cell b holds a desperate merchant
Cell c contains two harmless skeletons of humans or elves

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: Common room occupied by three bugbears. It is furnished with common rattan furniture, including tables and chairs, along with heavy wooden bunks.

areas.name: Owlbear
areas.description: Behind the door, listening reveals grunting and snuffling. Chained to the east wall is a great owlbear, captured as a cub and raised by the bugbears. It considers the lair its home and defends it ferociously against intruders. The chain is weakly attached to the wall and can easily be ripped free. The bugbears sometimes allow it to roam free and often take it outside with them.

features.description: Door from which grunting and snuffling can be heard
Chain fixed to the east wall
Weak chain attachment that the owlbear can rip free

areas.name: Main Boss
areas.description: Main chamber of the head bugbear and his small guard, furnished with heavy wooden beds, chairs, and tables. The chief wears a necklace bearing 300 gp and has two keys on a thong around one wrist: one opens the locked door to the west, and the other opens the treasure room (64). The locked west door is stout, thick, and iron-bound, but the room beyond it is empty.

features.description: Stout, thick, iron-bound locked door to the west leading to an empty room

areas.name: Entrance
areas.description: An apparently unguarded entranceway. A dead goblin and two dead bugbears lie sprawled outside, dead for several days and only nibbled by small animals and birds. The area is quiet, reeks of desolation, and any tracks are days old. This is a trap: gnolls from guard posts 70 and 71 watch around the corner at area "w" and try to end-round intruders depending on what they do.

features.description: Two dead bugbears outside the entrance

effect.manual: The entrance is a lure. Gnolls from 70 and 71 keep watch at area "w"; if intruders investigate room 70, gnolls from 70 rush from the west opening, while those in 71 may use a well-concealed secret door to attack from behind.

areas.name: Guard Post
areas.description: A shabby guard post with three crude benches carved from sections of a large tree. One gnoll is on duty at the corner marked "w" with the one from room 71 and alerts the others here if intruders are detected. Each gnoll has 1d6 ep.

features.description: Three crude benches carved from large tree sections

areas.name: Guard Post
areas.description: A shabby guard post. One gnoll is on duty at the corner marked "w" with the one from room 70 and alerts the others here if intruders are spotted. Each gnoll has 1d6 ep.

areas.name: Common Room
areas.description: A common room where gnolls lounge, often bored and bickering. A pet wolf is tied by rope to the northwest corner, fed scraps, and trained as both guard and war dog. It has a high chance of hearing or smelling anyone lingering outside the doors. Each gnoll has 1d6 ep. The unmarked room to the southwest contains crude cots.

features.description: Pet wolf tied by rope to the northwest corner
Unmarked room to the southwest with crude cots

areas.name: Cavern
areas.description: A natural cavern divided by stone columns. There is nothing here, though dripping water forms pools of clean drinking water.

areas.name: Leader's Room
areas.description: The gnoll leader resides here with two mates. The leader fights with a Battle Axe +1 and wears a golden necklace set with gems worth 700 gp. The room is cluttered with junk, including many clay drinking jars, many smashed. One jar contains two keys tied together; they open the Treasure Hoard to the south and the Storeroom at 75.

features.description: Collection of clay drinking jars, many smashed

areas.name: Treasure Hoard
areas.description: The leader keeps a giant black widow spider here, feeding it rats and kobolds as needed and cleaning up after it. The spider lurks overhead in webs so dust-covered they appear to be the ceiling about 10 feet up, while the actual ceiling is 15 feet high. It avoids the door trap after a bad experience with it. A strong chest and other boxes fill the room.

features.description: Dust-covered overhead webs about 10' up that resemble the ceiling

effect.manual: The door is trapped with a heavy flint axe-head on a strong wooden bar that swings down, attacking as a 3 HD monster and dealing 1d8+2 damage on a hit.

areas.name: Storeroom
areas.description: A crammed storeroom full of barrels, boxes, and bags. Most contain food or cheap ale. The gnoll leader in room 74 has the key.

features.description: Most stores are food or cheap ale

areas.name: Dungeon
areas.description: A dungeon with a gnoll guard carrying the key and 1d6 ep. Captives kept for ransom are held here, though there are no prisoners now. Cell "a" is a common cell, and cell "b" is for segregated prisoners. Area "c" is reached by climbing rough-cut steps about 10 feet up and contains a torture area with a chopping block, hand axe, wooden rack, several wooden sawhorses, a pile of coal, an iron brazier, and crude iron pokers.

features.description: Cell doors made of thick wooden bars with 1-inch gaps
Iron hinges and locks on cell doors
Locks are poor quality and easy for a thief to pick
Area "c" reached by rough-cut steps 10' up

areas.name: Gateway Flanked by Towers
areas.description: A corroded brass plaque over the gates reads "Roslof Manor." The old wooden gates were torn aside and battered down long ago in a forgotten fight that led to the manor being abandoned. Recently, someone removed the stronger timbers and much of the metal hardware; the rest is laid out in a pattern as if plans are being made to replace them. The area has been cleaned up somewhat for easy access. Hoof prints and wagon tracks lead in and out across soft earth amid badly broken paving stones.

features.description: Ruined wooden gates with remaining timbers and metal hardware laid out as if for replacement

areas.name: West Gate Tower
areas.description: This gate tower was three stories high, with the roof as a fourth, but the top floors have collapsed inward, leaving only the bottom level. It is a simple hollow tube with a steep stairway that would have accessed each floor if they were intact. Arrow slits occur every 10 feet and face outward. The entrance door has a lock but is not kept locked; a heavy bar lies beside it to fit brackets on the frame. This tower serves as a guard post for human fighters wearing scarlet cloaks, red-enameled helmets, and chain mail. They are currently dealing with a giant black widow spider that crawled into the rubble overhead and may scuttle down the wall to attack.

features.description: Steep interior stairway to ruined upper levels
Arrow slits every 10 feet facing outward
Heavy bar for the entrance door

areas.name: East Gate Tower
areas.description: As area 78, but this tower has been badly damaged and is not safe to use; no humans are stationed here. The door once had a lock, but it has been broken off its hinges and leans askew in the frame, wedged in place by heavy wooden pegs. The lower floor is occupied by giant centipedes amid the rubble. The rubble of the next floor is overrun with giant rats among broken furniture and harmless skeletal remains.

features.description: Broken door wedged into frame with heavy wooden pegs
Rubble on lower level and collapsed upper level

areas.name: Stables
areas.description: These stables are ruined by neglect. They once included a smithy, small cottages, hay storage, wagon storage, rooms for grooms, and similar outbuildings. The structures have collapsed into a maze of darkness and ruin. Soot and burned timbers from ancient fires are everywhere, and new weeds grow through the rubbish. A giant weasel is sparring with three giant shrews that have killed a pack of giant rats and intend to feast on them; if they smell fresh meat, they attack that instead.

features.description: Collapsed outbuildings forming a maze of darkness and ruin
Soot and burned timbers from ancient fires
Carcasses of giant rats killed by the shrews

areas.name: Cottages
areas.description: These were once quarters for gardeners and other staff, but are now ruins much like area 80. Berries, fruit trees, and vegetables grow wild here. During the growing season, characters can easily gather 1d6 weeks of rations, though most will spoil within a week or two unless dried or otherwise preserved.

features.description: Wild berries, fruit trees, and vegetables

areas.name: North Wall
areas.description: This stretch of the north wall is marked by rotten wooden buildings and weeds where dog kennels once stood. The wall here is patrolled by a minotaur allied with the humans. If it notices intruders, it bellows for guards, throws rocks for 1d6 rounds or as reasonable, then charges down the nearest steps. In the northeast corner stands a rude lean-to of hides sheltering the half-eaten raw carcass of a deer, with various animal parts strewn about.

features.description: Rotten wooden kennel buildings and weeds
Rude lean-to of hides in the northeast corner

areas.name: Moat
areas.description: The main house relies on a 10-foot-deep moat for security, currently full of water. A simple wooden bridge once crossed it at the front entrance, but it burned down long ago, leaving only footing planks and timbers on each side. The moat is fed by a slow-moving stream entering under the north wall and exiting to the east. Each opening has an arched undercut with two sets of heavy iron bars, one on each side, to keep out intruders.

features.description: Remains of burned wooden bridge footings
Slow-moving stream entering under the north wall and exiting east
Arched undercuts with two sets of heavy iron bars at each stream opening

areas.name: Main Doors
areas.description: The great iron double doors of the main house are firmly shut and barred from the inside; short of using a massive ram, they cannot be opened. High, wide windows line the walls, secured by heavy iron bars that admit nothing larger than a squirrel. Ripping out the bars or making another noisy entry would likely attract attention from inside. On the west side of the door, some wall blocks can be easily pulled out: invaders once knocked a hole there, and the current occupants restacked the blocks sloppily. Characters can reopen the breach and step inside into room 85. Off to one side are three wooden ramps, each about 24 feet long and made from collected timbers and iron hardware, allowing wagons to cross the moat.

features.description: Great iron double doors barred from inside
Loose wall blocks on the west side that can be removed to make an entry hole
Three wooden ramps about 24 feet long for wagons to cross the moat

areas.name: Main Hall
areas.description: The manor's lower floor has been heavily used. Many hardwood timbers are torn out or scuffed, and dirt is everywhere, while upstairs is cleaner. A heavy iron chandelier hangs overhead for lanterns or torches, and small wall mounts are placed throughout the manor. Skylights illuminate the main hall by day. Two ornate stairways, marked "a" and "b," rise about 20 feet to the second-floor balcony at area 98. Under the balcony are swinging double doors leading into the back. The main hall ceiling is about 30 feet high; other rooms on this floor have 20-foot ceilings. Recent bootprints in the dust lead everywhere. Some walls of adjoining rooms were once thick hardwood but have been torn down in places. Horses can be heard in areas 86 and 87. As adventurers enter, three fighters in red surcoats over chain mail and carrying swords come down the stairs, discussing whether to raid towns or waylay travelers. One is a woman and wields a longsword +1. They may try to lure intruders into an ambush by sending one to area 88 while the others lead the party upstairs to area 106 before attacking. A smith and two assistants in the stables join them if called or if fighting is heard.

features.description: Wall mounts for lanterns or torches
Ornate stairs "a" and "b" to the second-floor balcony
Swinging double doors under the balcony

areas.name: Renovated Stables
areas.description: These rooms were once a library, music room, and gymnasium, but have been gutted and fitted with simple wooden stalls to serve as smithy and stables. There are four riding horses, three mules, and three oxen here. Nearby are hay, feed bags, sacks of feed grain, and other supplies. In one corner stand a small traveling anvil, a pile of bricks, bags of coal, several hammers, other tools, and a few horseshoes. Two horses were previously lost to wandering monsters before the remaining animals were brought inside for safety.

features.description: Hay, feed bags, and sacks of feed grain

areas.name: Wagon Storage
areas.description: The south end of this area was once a posh sitting room, but the walls were knocked out to make room for wagons and equipment. Two wagons and two carts are stored here, along with boxes, tarps, and other items. The northern end was once a long dining hall. Old smashed tables and chairs are piled in neat stacks like firewood in short lengths. Some of the stronger, thicker pieces are arranged like building timbers ready for use. There is plenty of room between the piles to move to and from the kitchen and prep room in back.

features.description: Stacks of smashed tables and chairs
Heavier wood pieces arranged like building timbers

areas.name: Prep Room
areas.description: Formerly a prep room for meals and a buffer for the noise and activity of the kitchen, this room now holds tables and chairs, usually cluttered with dirty wooden plates, pewter or wooden mugs, and similar items. A keg of cheap beer sits propped on a table in one corner. A group of men are seated here eating bread, meat, gravy, and cheap beer. If fighting breaks out, two more men run in from the kitchen in area 89. The leader wears chain mail and carries a sword; the others wear red-stained leather armor and carry assorted weapons such as short swords, hand axes, and war hammers.

areas.name: Kitchen
areas.description: This kitchen is equipped to cook large meals, with several ovens and stoves along the outer walls. There are plenty of tables, sinks, and dirty wooden dishes. Two men are here cooking stew on one of the stoves. If a fight breaks out, they join the men in room 88. They are armed with hand axes and wear red-stained leather armor.

areas.name: Store Room
areas.description: A storeroom for dry foods and similar supplies. Bags of flour, other grains, and vegetables are stacked here. A narrow set of stairs descends 10 feet to a cold room where fresh carcasses of venison, boar, rabbits, and other game animals hang from iron hooks.

features.description: Stacks of flour, grain, and vegetables
Narrow stairs descending 10 feet to a cold room
Cold room with fresh carcasses of venison, boar, rabbits, and other game hanging on iron hooks

areas.name: Laundry Room
areas.description: This was once the laundry room, formerly filled with buckets and tubs. Now only long ropes for hanging laundry remain, and wooden shelves for linens and rugs stand empty. In one corner are two sealed buckets, one containing red paint and the other red varnish.

features.description: Empty wooden shelves for linens and rugs

areas.name: Wash Room
areas.description: A wash room for people, clothes, dishes, and the like. It contains bath tubs, cloth screens on wooden frames, and a table with bars of soap.

areas.name: Back Door
areas.description: The rear exit of the manor. The door is a heavy security door with two iron bars that can be thrown across it from the inside.

features.description: Two iron bars that secure it from the inside

areas.name: Servant Quarters
areas.description: One of the enlarged servant quarters, now partly used by foot troops. The inner partitions in this set of rooms have been torn down to enlarge it. In this room, two men are resting after a fight with giant rats. They can still fight and accost intruders as best they can. They are not wearing their leather armor, though they can put it on if given time.

features.description: Enlarged servant quarters with inner partitions torn down

areas.name: Servant Quarters
areas.description: Servant quarters, enlarged by tearing down the inner partitions, now occupied in part by foot troops, most of whom are eating or elsewhere. (The module keys 94 to 97 as one shared entry.)

features.description: Enlarged servant quarters with inner partitions torn down

areas.name: Servant Quarters
areas.description: Servant quarters, enlarged by tearing down the inner partitions, now occupied in part by foot troops, most of whom are eating or elsewhere. (The module keys 94 to 97 as one shared entry.)

features.description: Enlarged servant quarters with inner partitions torn down

areas.name: Servant Quarters
areas.description: One of the enlarged servant quarters, now partly used by foot troops. As adventurers enter the hall around this room, a man comes out the door and, unless stopped, ducks back inside and calls for help. Four men occupy this room, asleep after watch. Their spears and hand axes are nearby. They are not currently wearing their red-stained leather armor, but will put it on if given time. Each has 2d6 gp on him.

features.description: Enlarged servant quarters with inner partitions torn down

areas.name: Stairway
areas.description: Stairway on the upper floor with a safety railing along the side. The stairs descend 20' to the ground floor at area #85. Ceilings on this floor are about 10' high.

areas.name: Guest Room
areas.description: Guest room serving as the residence of the female fighter and one of the male fighters met coming down the stairs in area #85. Furnished with a makeshift bed, table, chairs, and similar basics.

features.description: Locked casket with a crude lock intended mainly to show tampering

areas.name: Guest Room
areas.description: Guest room occupied by one of the three fighters encountered on the stairs in area #85. Furnished with a makeshift bed, table, chairs, and such. A sack of valuables is hidden under the bed, and the room's owner keeps a pet snake there to guard it; it may immediately grab and pull under anyone who investigates unwisely.

areas.name: Guest Room
areas.description: Guest room now used by one of the clerics as a private room; see area #106. It has makeshift furnishings including a bed, table, chairs, and similar basics. On a chest of drawers are religious items arranged in worshipful fashion around an evil golden icon.

features.description: Religious display arranged on the chest of drawers

valuables.name: golden icon of an evil demonic being

areas.name: Guest Room
areas.description: Guest room claimed by one of the clerics as a private room; see area #106. It contains shabby, slapped-together furniture: bed, table, chairs, and such. A painting of horrors and stark terror hangs on one wall; it has little general value, though a good church might pay for it in order to destroy it or use it as an instructional example of evil. Beneath it hang looted religious valuables.

features.description: Painting of horrors and stark terror hung on the wall

areas.name: Guest Room
areas.description: Guest room now used by the Magic-User as a private room; see area #106. Furnishings are unremarkable: makeshift bed, table, chairs, and such. The beginnings of an alchemical laboratory for making potions are here, but it is incomplete.

features.description: Incomplete alchemical laboratory for making potions

areas.name: Guest Room
areas.description: Guest room used as storage for various items kept for future use.

areas.name: Children's Nursery
areas.description: Former bedroom and nursery for children. The double doors to this room hang open. A few old toys and cribs lie scattered about under dust.

areas.name: Master Room
areas.description: Lavish, very large former master room now serving as the headquarters and treasury of the band. The door is shut, and voices can be heard inside. Three humans are leaning over a map on a table, planning to use monsters to carve out their own empire; they attack intruders unless the intruders surrender. Several gaslights fed from natural gas taps illuminate the room. Furnishings are sparse because the old ones were looted long ago: a large round table, some chairs, and a desk. The nearby spell book of the magic-user contains the spells he knows.

features.description: Door with a warning bell hung inside near the top
Several gaslights fed from natural gas taps
Two large chests holding war funds

effect.manual: A small bell hung from a rod on the inside near the top of the door jingles if the door is not opened carefully. The magic-user's spell book has a needle trap in the cover; save vs. Poison or die.
